title: POC Weekly Sync: Quantization Experiments (INT8 / FP8)
summary: Weekly pilot sync to review INT8 / FP8 quantization results on the NIM-XL model subset. Reviewed perf deltas (latency, throughput), token-accuracy/regression checks on eval prompt sets, and next steps for additional micro-benchmarks and quality gates. Customer is leaning toward a two-track approach: INT8 on dedicated for cost-savings and FP8 on private for critical queries. Action items captured for Redwood to share full perf artifacts and for customer to run additional evals on long-tail prompts.
topics: Recap of last week - INT8 baseline vs FP8
Perf numbers: P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU VRAM
Quality impact: exact-match, BLEU-ish checks, hallucination cases
Deployment tradeoffs: Dedicated vs Private, KMS requirements
questions: Can Redwood reproduce FP8 regressions on our long-form prompts?
What are the recommended safety/rollback policies for canarying quantized models?
Do we need special kernel builds for our TPU-like instances?
action_items: Alex Kim: Send complete perf spreadsheet (INT8 vs FP8) + raw latency traces and config used (due: 2025-08-22)
Priya Desai: Produce per-prompt delta report highlighting top 20 regressions and suggested mitigation (due: 2025-08-25)
Maya Chen: Run customer-side long tail eval set (5k prompts) and share results in the shared drive (due: 2025-08-26)
Tom Alvarez: Provision dedicated test cluster with same CUDA driver as prod and grant access to Redwood team (due: 2025-08-21)
Jordan Lee: Schedule follow-up benchmark session with infra & infra perf (due: 2025-08-28)
next_steps: Redwood to email perf artifacts and PR curves
Customer to run long-tail eval and flag regressions
Joint run of micro-benchmarks on customer infra next week
Decision meeting after extra evals to pick INT8 vs FP8 rollout strategy
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-19 16:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Maya (Nimbus Head of ML), Tom (Infra), Rahul (Data)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday afternoon, quick check in on the quant experiments. Maya, how's your morning — or, you know, afternoon over there?
[00:18] Maya: Afternoon, yeah, pretty good. We ran the INT8 set across the 2-node dedicated pool last night. I wanted to go over the numbers, we saw the cost down obviously but a handful of prompts with weird drop in fidelity.
[00:31] Priya: Cool. We'll go through the perf and the delta table we posted. Quick remind, the configs we ran: INT8 with per-channel symmetrical quant, FP8 using the new bfloat-ish prototype we called FP8-s. Might be a few name mismatches in the sheets, sorry for that.
[00:50] Tom: One note: our test cluster uses driver 525, is that what you tested on?
[00:59] Priya: We used 528 in Redwood lab, small diff but could affect kernels. We'll note that.
[01:10] Rahul: The big thing for us is P95 latency for customer-facing flows, anything above 250ms is risky.
[01:18] Alex: Right. Short recap — INT8 brought token cost down ~34% on avg and improved throughput by 1.8x in batching scenarios. Latency P95 actually improved in small-batch workloads but in long-seq cases we saw some stalling due to cache micro-behaviour.
[01:38] Maya: Yeah and FP8? We ran a subset and saw slightly better numeric quality on some generative tasks but the hallucination rate changed on some of our evaluation prompts.
[01:49] Priya: For FP8, the average token-level perplexity improved slightly in our internal eval, but principled metrics like exact-match on code-style prompts dropped on ~0.7% of cases. Not huge but you flagged those as important.
[02:05] Alex: Quick question: do you have examples of the top regressions? We included a top-10 in the artifact but it's noisy.
[02:12] Maya: Yes we uploaded three example prompts to the shared folder, one is a long-form legal-style prompt that the model starts inventing new facts under FP8.
[02:23] Priya: That's helpful. We suspect quantization scaling on attention keys is shifting some logits for long contexts. We have mitigations: hybrid precision for attention + FP8 for FFN, or bias-correction fine-tune on a small prompt set.
[02:41] Tom: Hybrid sounds reasonable but does it add a lot of memory overhead?
[02:48] Priya: Minimal — maybe 1-2% VRAM increase, but you'd regain most of the FP8 quality while keeping cost savings.
[03:00] Alex: Also worth noting rollout strategy: canary about 5% of traffic to quantized variant with automatic rollback on quality regressions flagged by evaluation hooks.
[03:12] Maya: Can Redwood hook into our eval pipeline? We prefer the quality gate to be in our CI.
[03:18] Jordan: Yes, we can integrate with your eval; we have an API to push prompt sets and get back per-prompt diffs. We'll need access and the dataset, that's in the action items.
[03:30] Rahul: One operational question — KMS and key rotation. For private we need BYOK and HSM. Does Redwood support that on FP8 runs?
[03:41] Alex: Yes, Private deployments can be integrated with customer KMS/HSM. There is no difference in encryption for quantized model weights — it's at rest and in transit as usual. We'll share the compliance doc.
[03:53] Maya: Ok, on the perf numbers — can you run an additional micro-benchmark with 4k tokens sequences? A lot of our workload is multi-turn long-doc summarization.
[04:03] Priya: We planned that. We'll run INT8/FP8 4k token runs, measure P50/P90/P95, and include GPU util and KV-cache hit rates.
[04:14] Tom: For the GPU util, also show concurrencies e.g., 8 inflight requests vs 1.
[04:20] Priya: Yep will include.

[06:12] Maya: A small nit: some model names in the artifacts say RedWood instead of Redwood, minor transcription.
[06:19] Alex: Ha yeah, classic speech-to-text. Noted.

[06:30] Priya: Quick call out on the numbers: INT8 batch throughput 2.1x on A100-40, P95 latency decreased by ~18ms for short sequences, but for 2k+ tokens P95 increased in a few cases due to decode step variance. FP8 had better stability on decode but had those quality dips in a small subset.
[06:56] Rahul: Did you test INT8 with per-channel vs per-tensor? We saw per-tensor caused more regressions.
[07:04] Priya: Per-channel wins for attention/FFN in general. Per-tensor is faster in some kernels but worse quality.
[07:12] Alex: On the cost model: even with a small VRAM bump for hybrid, INT8 hybrid still gives ~28% cost reduction vs float16 baseline depending on utilization.
[07:25] Maya: Can you produce cost delta per 1M tokens for our current traffic shapes? That's helpful for the business case.
[07:32] Alex: Yes, we'll add a cost-per-token table in the spreadsheet.

[10:00] Tom: About the canary and rollback: if we route 5% and detect regression, what's the time to roll back?
[10:08] Jordan: We have automated rollback hooks; typical rollbacks are immediate once the monitor triggers — under a minute to fail traffic back to the stable variant.
[10:17] Maya: For the quality monitors, can we tune thresholds per prompt-type? Our legal prompts are very sensitive.
[10:24] Priya: Absolutely, per-route thresholds and per-prompt gating is supported. We can also tie to manual approval for sensitive routes.

[14:00] Rahul: We noticed a mismatch in the tokenizer behavior in FP8 runs, some whitespace tokens changed in probability distribution; could that be a tokeniser bug?
[14:10] Priya: More likely numerical noise causing different argmax behaviours; tokeniser should be stable but we'll double-check the tokenization pipeline used during quantization.
[14:22] Maya: Also, is there a recommended retrain or calib step for FP8? We didn't calibrate on our dataset beyond a small holdout.
[14:30] Priya: We have a light calibration step and a bias-correction pass that helps. For FP8 especially, a tiny fine-tune on representative prompts (10k steps) often eliminates the worst regressions.
[14:42] Alex: We'll propose a conservative path: INT8 for non-sensitive routes first, FP8 reserved for compute-heavy internal batch jobs where hallucination tolerance is higher, or FP8 hybrid for customer-facing with extra QC.

[20:00] Maya: Timing and stakeholders — we're aiming to decide by end of month for a limited pilot. Main stakeholders: product + legal + infra. Security wants SOC2 artifacts and KMS notes.
[20:12] Alex: We'll include SOC2 checklist and the KMS integration guide in the follow-up email.

[26:00] Priya: One more thing — the per-prompt delta report will include suggested mitigations: keep bias terms in FP32, hybrid attention, or small fine-tune. We'll rank by expected ROI.
[26:30] Rahul: For the ROI, please include expected token cost decrease vs additional infra or engineering time.
[26:38] Priya: Sure.

[31:00] Maya: Are there any blockers from Redwood's side to do the next micro-benchmark on our infrastructure?
[31:07] Alex: We'll need the driver/mk versions and SSH jumpbox access; otherwise we can run remote micro-benchmarks from our env against a captive cluster.
[31:18] Tom: I'll create the jumpbox creds and add Redwood team. Expect an email by Thursday.

[36:00] Jordan: Summarizing next steps: Redwood sends full perf artifacts and per-prompt deltas; customer runs long-tail eval and provisions cluster; follow-up call scheduled for Aug 28 to review results and make decision.
[36:15] Maya: That works.

[40:00] Alex: Anything else? If not, thanks everyone, we'll circulate notes and action items.
[40:07] Maya: Thanks all.
[40:09] Tom: Thanks.
[40:10] Rahul: Thanks.

End of recording"
